questions.q: What is −5 in 8-bit two's complement?
How many characters can 8-bit extended ASCII represent?
questions.why: 2⁸ = 256; standard ASCII uses 7 bits (128).

questions.q: Increasing the sampling rate of a sound file…
questions.why: More samples per second capture the sound more accurately.

questions.q: Run-length encoding of a bitmap image compresses:
o: Repeated characters in a text file
Runs of consecutive pixels of the same colour
questions.why: Examiners (2023): some described compressing a text file using characters instead of colours.

questions.q: How is the two's complement of a binary integer obtained?
o: Invert all bits (one's complement) and add 1
questions.why: Two's complement allows signed addition and subtraction with standard binary adder circuits: invert bits, then add 1.

long.q: Convert the denary number −45 into an 8-bit two's complement binary integer. Show your working.
scheme: M1: invert the bits: 11010010

long.q: A bitmap image is 1024 × 768 pixels with a colour depth of 24 bits. Calculate the file size in mebibytes (MiB), ignoring any header.
scheme: M1: 1024 × 768 × 24 bits, or × 3 bytes

questions.q: Which topology connects every device to a central node?
questions.why: A failure of the central switch stops the network.

questions.q: What does CSMA/CD help with on a shared medium?
questions.why: Devices listen before sending and back off after a collision.

questions.q: Which is a characteristic, rather than a benefit, of a LAN?
o: It covers a small geographical area
Users can share files and printers
It gives every computer internet access
questions.why: Examiners (2023): there was confusion between benefits and characteristics, and 'a LAN gives internet access' was common.

questions.q: An IPv4 address is split into which two parts?
questions.why: Examiners (2023): 'Network IP and Host IP' instead of 'Network ID and Host ID' was a common error.

questions.q: Which protocol in the TCP/IP stack is responsible for resolving a domain name into an IP address?
questions.why: The Domain Name System (DNS) translates human-readable hostnames (e.g. panalo.app) into IP addresses.

questions.q: Which memory must be refreshed constantly?
questions.why: DRAM stores bits as charge in capacitors, which leaks.

questions.q: A logic circuit outputs 1 when exactly one input is 1. It is…
questions.why: XOR is exclusive OR.

questions.q: Which type of memory must be refreshed constantly?
questions.why: DRAM stores bits as charge in capacitors, which leaks away.

questions.q: For which inputs is X = (A NAND B) AND C equal to 1?
questions.why: A NAND B is 1 unless both A and B are 1, and C must also be 1; only A = 0, B = 1, C = 1 meets both conditions.

questions.q: A device's firmware must be updatable by the user downloading a new version, without removing the chip from the circuit board. Which memory should hold it?
questions.why: EEPROM can be erased and rewritten electrically while in the circuit; EPROM must be removed and erased with ultraviolet light, PROM can be written only once, and SRAM is volatile.

long.q: Describe two differences between static RAM (SRAM) and dynamic RAM (DRAM).
scheme: B1: SRAM uses flip-flops; DRAM stores bits as charge in capacitors
B1: DRAM must be refreshed regularly; SRAM does not
B1: SRAM is faster to access, so it is used for cache
B1: DRAM is cheaper per bit and denser, so it is used for main memory

questions.q: In the fetch–execute cycle, what happens first?
o: The address in the PC is copied to the MAR
questions.why: MAR ← [PC]; then MDR ← memory; CIR ← [MDR]; PC incremented.

questions.q: Which addressing mode uses the operand as the actual value?
questions.why: Direct uses it as an address; immediate uses it as the value.

questions.q: Which describes the control bus?
o: It carries control and timing signals between components
questions.why: Examiners (2023): answers often said the control bus carries data or instructions; both are wrong.

questions.q: What is the purpose of the Program Counter (PC) in the Von Neumann architecture?
o: It counts how many programs are currently running
It holds the current instruction being executed
It holds the memory address of the next instruction to be fetched
questions.why: The PC points to the memory address of the next instruction; it is automatically incremented during the fetch phase.

questions.q: The accumulator holds 00010110. What does it hold after the instruction LSL #2?
questions.why: A logical shift left by 2 moves every bit two places left and fills the right with zeros, multiplying 22 by 4 to give 88 (01011000).

long.q: Describe the roles of the program counter (PC) and the memory address register (MAR) in the fetch stage of the fetch–execute cycle.
scheme: B1: the PC holds the address of the next instruction
B1: this address is copied to the MAR
B1: the instruction at the address in the MAR is fetched into the MDR (then CIR)
B1: the PC is incremented to point to the next instruction

questions.q: Which is a benefit of an interpreter while developing code?
o: Errors are reported as each line runs, making debugging easier
questions.why: Compilers produce faster executables but report errors after compiling.

questions.q: Which is a utility program?
questions.why: Utilities help maintain the computer; others are applications or translators.

questions.q: What does a linker do?
o: Combines object code and library routines into one executable
Translates source code line by line
questions.why: A loader then copies the executable into memory.

questions.q: Which is a benefit of a program using a dynamic link library (DLL) rather than having the library code compiled into it?
o: The program can run even if the DLL file is missing
The executable file is smaller and the library can be updated without recompiling the program
The library code is copied into every program that uses it
The program can no longer have run-time errors
questions.why: A DLL is linked when the program runs, so its code is not stored in the executable and several programs can share one updated copy; the program fails if the DLL is missing.

questions.q: Which IDE feature lets a programmer run a program one statement at a time while checking the values of variables?
o: Single stepping with a variable watch window
questions.why: Single stepping runs one line at a time and a watch window shows variable values as they change, which helps locate logic errors; the others help while typing code.

questions.q: A firewall…
o: filters network traffic based on rules
questions.why: It allows or blocks traffic between networks.

questions.q: A check digit is used for…
questions.why: It is calculated from the other digits, e.g. ISBN.

questions.q: What does a firewall do?
o: Encrypts all data on a disk
Checks incoming and outgoing traffic against rules and blocks what is not allowed
questions.why: It sits between a network and the outside world.

questions.q: A hospital makes sure that only a patient's own doctors can view that patient's records. Which concept does this mainly protect?
questions.why: Data privacy means keeping personal data away from people who are not entitled to see it; integrity is about the data staying accurate and consistent.

questions.q: Which error would NOT be detected by a parity check on a byte?
o: Two bits changed in the same byte
The parity bit itself being flipped
Three bits changed in the same byte
questions.why: Changing two bits leaves the number of 1s odd or even as before, so the parity still matches; any odd number of changed bits is detected.

questions.q: Open-source software…
o: makes its source code available to view and modify under a licence
is always free of all conditions
questions.why: Licences like GPL set conditions on sharing changes.

questions.q: Which statement about free software is correct?
o: Users may run, study, modify and share it; the source code is available
It is always free of charge but you cannot see the source code
It is the same as freeware
questions.why: Examiners (2023): there was confusion between freeware and free software.

questions.q: Which licence lets users study, modify and redistribute source code?
questions.why: Freeware is free to use but usually without the source code.

questions.q: A program can be downloaded and used free for 30 days, after which the user must pay to keep using it. Which type of licence is this?
o: Free software (as defined by the Free Software Foundation)
questions.why: Shareware is given out free for a trial period or with limited features, and the user pays to continue; freeware is free to use with no charge at all.

questions.q: A software engineer finds a safety flaw in a product, but her manager tells her to release it on time. Which principle of the ACM/IEEE Software Engineering Code of Ethics should guide her most?
o: Client and employer: always do what the employer instructs
Self: keep up to date with new technologies
Public: act consistently with the public interest
questions.why: Engineers must not release software that could harm the public, even when an employer asks; serving the employer has to be consistent with the public interest.

questions.q: A table is in 1NF when…
o: it has no repeating groups and every field is atomic
questions.why: 2NF removes partial dependencies; 3NF removes transitive ones.

questions.q: A foreign key…
o: uniquely identifies records in its own table
links to the primary key of another table
questions.why: It creates the relationship between tables.

questions.q: In a relational table, a tuple is:
questions.why: Examiners (2023): there was considerable confusion between rows and columns.

questions.q: In relational database design, what is a composite primary key?
o: A primary key that references a foreign key table
A primary key encrypted with a hash
A primary key formed by combining two or more attributes
questions.why: A composite key combines multiple columns to uniquely identify a record when no single column alone is unique.

questions.q: A table ORDER_LINE(OrderID, ProductID, Quantity, ProductName) has the composite key (OrderID, ProductID). ProductName depends only on ProductID. Which normal form does the table fail to meet?
o: None: it is already fully normalised
questions.why: ProductName depends on only part of the composite key, which is a partial dependency, so the table is in 1NF but not 2NF.

long.q: Explain what is meant by a foreign key, with an example from a school database with the tables STUDENT and CLASS.
scheme: B1: an attribute in one table that is the primary key of another table
B1: it is used to create a relationship between the two tables
B1: e.g. ClassID in STUDENT links to ClassID, the primary key of CLASS

questions.q: Abstraction means…
o: removing unnecessary detail to focus on what matters
questions.why: Decomposition, by contrast, breaks a problem into parts.

questions.q: FOR Count ← 1 TO 10 … NEXT Count. Which statement should not be inside the loop?
questions.why: Examiners (2023): FOR loops sometimes added an extra increment, so the loop ran the wrong number of times.

questions.q: What does a structure chart show?
o: The modules of a program, their hierarchy and the parameters passed
The data stored in a table
questions.why: Arrows show data and flags passed between modules.

questions.q: What is output? Count ← 0 ; FOR i ← 1 TO 10 ; IF i MOD 3 = 0 THEN Count ← Count + i ENDIF ; NEXT i ; OUTPUT Count
questions.why: Only i = 3, 6 and 9 are multiples of 3, and their values are added: 3 + 6 + 9 = 18. 3 would be how many multiples there are, not their sum.

questions.q: What is output? X ← 100 ; Steps ← 0 ; WHILE X > 1 ; X ← X DIV 2 ; Steps ← Steps + 1 ; ENDWHILE ; OUTPUT Steps
questions.why: X goes 100, 50, 25, 12, 6, 3, 1 (DIV discards the remainder), which is six passes; the loop then stops because 1 > 1 is false.

long.q: Write pseudocode for a function LinearSearch(Items, Target) that returns the index of Target in the 1D array Items[1:100], or −1 if it is not found.
scheme: M1: function header with parameters and RETURNS INTEGER
M1: a loop over indices 1 to 100
M1: compares Items[Index] with Target
M1: returns Index as soon as it is found
M1: returns −1 after the loop if not found

questions.q: A stack works on which principle?
questions.why: Last in, first out; a queue is first in, first out.

questions.q: Which abstract data type is first in, first out?
questions.why: A stack is last in, first out.

questions.q: An item is added to a circular queue that is not full. What changes?
o: All items move down one place
Only the rear pointer moves on (wrapping to the start if needed)
questions.why: Examiners (2023): many wrongly said existing contents must be moved.

questions.q: An empty stack has these operations applied: PUSH 4, PUSH 7, POP, PUSH 2, PUSH 9, POP. Which item is now at the top?
questions.why: POP removes the most recent item: 7 is removed, then 2 and 9 are pushed and 9 is removed, leaving 4 at the bottom and 2 on top.

questions.q: A node is deleted from the middle of a linked list held in arrays. What must change?
o: Every node after it is moved up one place in the array
The start pointer is set to null
The pointer in the previous node is changed to point to the node after the deleted one
Only the data item in the node is set to an empty string
questions.why: Linking the previous node past the deleted one removes it from the list without moving any data; the freed node is normally added to the free list.

long.q: A stack is held in a 1D array Stack[1:50] with a variable TopPointer (0 when empty). Describe how an item is pushed onto the stack.
scheme: B1: check whether the stack is full (TopPointer = 50)
B1: if full, report an error / do not add
B1: otherwise increment TopPointer by 1
B1: store the item at Stack[TopPointer]

questions.q: A function differs from a procedure because it…
questions.why: Both can take parameters; only a function returns a value.

questions.q: In pseudocode, a function gives back its result with:
questions.why: Examiners (2023): OUTPUT was often used in place of RETURN.

questions.q: Which pseudocode extracts 3 characters starting at position 2 of Name?
questions.why: Examiners (2023): LEFT() was used where MID() was needed.

questions.q: What is output? PROCEDURE Double(BYREF X : INTEGER) ; X ← X * 2 ; ENDPROCEDURE ; Num ← 5 ; CALL Double(Num) ; CALL Double(Num) ; OUTPUT Num
questions.why: BYREF passes the variable itself, so each call changes Num: 5 becomes 10 and then 20. With BYVAL only a copy would change and 5 would be output.

questions.q: Name ← "Cambridge". What is returned by MID(Name, LENGTH(Name) - 3, 3)?
questions.why: LENGTH(Name) is 9, so MID starts at position 9 − 3 = 6 and takes 3 characters: i, d, g.

questions.q: Which testing uses values at the edges of the valid range?
questions.why: Boundary data tests the limits, e.g. 0 and 100 for a percentage.

questions.q: A stub is used in testing to:
o: Stand in for a module that is not written yet, returning a simple value
questions.why: Examiners (2023): mistakes included calling stub testing integration testing or saying the dummy module 'checks' the program.

questions.q: Why is the waterfall model unsuitable when requirements may change?
o: Each stage is finished before the next, so going back is slow and costly
It is only for small programs
questions.why: Iterative and RAD models suit changing requirements.

questions.q: After release, a program is changed so that it works with a new version of the operating system. Which type of maintenance is this?
questions.why: Adaptive maintenance changes a program to cope with a changed environment such as new hardware, a new OS or new laws; corrective fixes bugs and perfective improves performance or features.

questions.q: Testers use their knowledge of the code to choose data so that every path through it is executed at least once. What type of testing is this?
questions.why: White-box testing uses the structure of the code to pick test data; black-box testing only compares inputs with expected outputs without looking at the code.

questions.q: Normalising a floating-point number…
o: gives the maximum precision for the mantissa size
questions.why: The first two mantissa bits differ (01 or 10), so no bits are wasted.

questions.q: Why are floating-point numbers normalised?
o: To give maximum precision and a unique representation
To use fewer bits for the exponent
questions.why: A normalised mantissa starts 01 (positive) or 10 (negative).

questions.q: More bits are given to the mantissa and fewer to the exponent. What happens?
questions.why: The mantissa sets precision; the exponent sets range.

questions.q: What happens if a calculation produces a positive floating-point number too small to be represented in the allocated bits?
questions.why: Underflow occurs when the magnitude of a non-zero value is closer to zero than the smallest representable non-zero float.

questions.q: A normalised floating-point number has an 8-bit two's complement mantissa 10100000 and a 4-bit two's complement exponent 0010. What is its denary value?
questions.why: The mantissa 1.0100000 is −1 + 0.25 = −0.75 and the exponent is 2, so the value is −0.75 × 2² = −3.

long.q: Normalise the floating-point number with an 8-bit two's complement mantissa 00010110 and a 4-bit exponent 0011, and state its denary value.
scheme: M1: mantissa 0.0010110, exponent 3
M1: shift mantissa left 2 places, exponent − 2
A1: mantissa 01011000, exponent 0001

questions.q: Which layer of TCP/IP routes packets between networks?
questions.why: IP at the Internet layer addresses and routes packets.

questions.q: Which protocol sends email from a client to a mail server?
questions.why: POP3 and IMAP retrieve email.

questions.q: What is true of packet switching?
o: All packets must take the same route
Packets may take different routes and are reassembled in order
questions.why: Circuit switching reserves a path for the whole communication.

questions.q: Which protocol keeps emails on the mail server so they can be read and organised from several devices?
questions.why: IMAP keeps the mailbox on the server and synchronises it, so every device sees the same messages; POP3 usually downloads and removes emails, and SMTP only sends mail.

questions.q: In the BitTorrent protocol, what is the role of a tracker?
o: It is a peer that holds the complete file and keeps uploading it
It is the file that contains all of the shared data
It is a router that gives torrent traffic priority
It is a server that keeps a record of which peers are sharing pieces of the file
questions.why: A tracker tells a new peer which other peers in the swarm hold pieces of the file; a peer with the whole file is a seed.

questions.q: RISC processors typically have…
o: a small set of simple instructions, often executed in one clock cycle
questions.why: This suits pipelining; CISC has many complex instructions.

questions.q: Which is a feature of RISC processors?
o: Simple instructions of fixed length, suited to pipelining
questions.why: CISC has complex instructions that may take several cycles.

questions.q: What is a virtual machine?
o: Software that emulates a computer, running on a host system
questions.why: It lets one machine run another OS, at a cost in performance.

questions.q: A processor has a 5-stage pipeline, each stage taking one clock cycle. With no hazards, how many clock cycles are needed to complete 6 instructions?
questions.why: The first instruction finishes after 5 cycles and then one more completes every cycle, so 5 + (6 − 1) = 10 cycles; without pipelining it would take 30.

questions.q: In a JK flip-flop, J = 1 and K = 1 when a clock pulse arrives. What happens to the output Q?
o: It toggles to the opposite state
It becomes invalid, as in an SR flip-flop with both inputs at 1
questions.why: J = K = 1 makes a JK flip-flop toggle on each clock pulse, which removes the invalid state an SR flip-flop has when both inputs are 1.

questions.q: Paging is a memory management technique that…
questions.why: Processes are split into pages that map to physical frames.

questions.q: What does the lexical analysis stage of compilation do?
o: Removes comments and white space and turns the source into tokens
Checks grammar against the language rules
questions.why: Syntax analysis comes next.

questions.q: In paging, memory is divided into:
o: Fixed-size blocks called pages and frames
questions.why: Segmentation uses variable-size blocks.

questions.q: What is the value of the Reverse Polish expression 6 2 3 + * ?
questions.why: 2 and 3 are added first to give 5, then 6 × 5 = 30; each operator acts on the two values directly before it on the stack.

questions.q: A running process requests data from a disk and must wait for it. Which state does the process move to?
questions.why: A process waiting for an I/O event is blocked; when the data arrives it moves to ready, not straight back to running, and waits for the scheduler.

questions.q: A digital signature is created using…
questions.why: Anyone can verify it with the sender's public key.

questions.q: Data sent to Asha is encrypted with which key?
questions.why: Examiners (2023): candidates confused public and private keys. Only Asha's private key can decrypt it.

questions.q: How is a digital signature produced?
o: The message is encrypted with the receiver's public key
The message is hashed and the hash is encrypted with the sender's private key
questions.why: Anyone can check it with the sender's public key.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of a digital certificate?
o: To encrypt a message with a shared symmetric key
To store the user's private key on a public server
To confirm that a public key belongs to a named organisation, signed by a certificate authority
To compress data before it is transmitted
questions.why: A certificate authority signs the certificate to vouch that the public key in it really belongs to that organisation, so others can trust it.

questions.q: Bob receives a message with a digital signature from Asha. Which key does Bob use to decrypt the signature and check the message digest?
questions.why: Asha encrypted the digest with her private key, so only her public key decrypts it; if it matches Bob's own hash of the message, the message is authentic and unchanged.

long.q: Explain how asymmetric encryption is used to send a confidential message.
scheme: B1: the receiver has a public key and a private key
B1: the sender encrypts with the receiver's public key
B1: only the receiver's private key can decrypt it
B1: the private key is never shared

questions.q: Dijkstra's algorithm finds…
o: the shortest path from one node to the others
questions.why: A* extends it with a heuristic.

questions.q: What does Dijkstra's algorithm find?
o: The shortest path from one node to the others in a weighted graph
The largest number in a list
A spanning tree of equal weights
questions.why: A* adds a heuristic to guide the search.

questions.q: In supervised learning, the training data are:
questions.why: Unsupervised learning finds patterns in unlabelled data.

questions.q: What distinguishes A* search from standard Dijkstra's algorithm?
o: A* uses an admissible heuristic function h(n) to estimate the cost to the goal
A* cannot find the shortest path
A* only works on trees with equal weights
questions.why: A* evaluates nodes using f(n) = g(n) + h(n), where h(n) is an admissible heuristic that never overestimates the distance to the goal.

questions.q: A program learns to play a game by being rewarded for good moves and penalised for bad ones. Which type of machine learning is this?
questions.why: Reinforcement learning improves by trial and error using rewards and penalties; supervised learning needs labelled examples of the correct outputs.

long.q: Describe how Dijkstra's algorithm finds the shortest path between two nodes.
scheme: B1: set the start node's distance to 0 and all others to infinity
B1: repeatedly visit the unvisited node with the smallest distance
B1: update neighbours' distances if a shorter path is found
B1: stop when the destination is visited; trace back for the path

questions.q: What is the time complexity of binary search?
questions.why: Each comparison halves the remaining items.

questions.q: Binary search needs the data to be:
questions.why: Each comparison halves the remaining data.

questions.q: What is the time complexity of a linear search?
questions.why: In the worst case every item is checked.

questions.q: A binary search looks for 23 in the sorted array [3, 8, 12, 15, 19, 23, 30, 41, 56] with indexes 1 to 9, using Mid ← (Low + High) DIV 2. Which values are compared with 23, in order?
questions.why: Mid = 5 gives 19 (too small, so Low = 6); Mid = 7 gives 30 (too large, so High = 6); Mid = 6 gives 23, which is found.

questions.q: FUNCTION F(N : INTEGER) RETURNS INTEGER ; IF N = 0 THEN RETURN 0 ELSE RETURN N + F(N - 1) ENDIF ; ENDFUNCTION. What does F(4) return?
questions.why: F(4) = 4 + F(3) = 4 + 3 + F(2) … = 4 + 3 + 2 + 1 + 0 = 10; the calls unwind once the base case F(0) returns 0.

questions.q: In OOP, inheritance allows…
o: a class to gain the attributes and methods of a parent class
one method to have many forms only
questions.why: Encapsulation hides data; polymorphism allows different behaviour for the same method.

questions.q: A subclass uses the attributes and methods of its superclass. This is:
questions.why: Polymorphism is redefining methods in subclasses.

questions.q: Why use exception handling?
o: To deal with run-time errors without the program crashing
questions.why: For example, a file that cannot be opened.

questions.q: Classes Circle and Square both inherit from Shape and each redefines the method Area(). Calling Area() on any Shape object runs the version for its own class. What is this called?
questions.why: Polymorphism lets a method with the same name behave differently for different classes, here by overriding; inheritance only explains why both classes have Area().

questions.q: Facts: parent(ann, bob). parent(bob, cara). Rule: grandparent(X, Z) IF parent(X, Y) AND parent(Y, Z). What is the result of the goal grandparent(ann, W)?
questions.why: X = ann matches parent(ann, bob), so Y = bob; parent(bob, Z) then gives Z = cara, so W = cara.

long.q: Write pseudocode for a recursive function Factorial(N) that returns N!.
scheme: M1: function header with parameter and return type
M1: base case IF N = 0 (or 1) RETURN 1
M1: ELSE RETURN N * Factorial(N − 1)
M1: correct ENDIF / ENDFUNCTION
